narrative.overview:
A quiet room with the lights down and one instrument panel lit. The ground is deep navy, panels are one step lighter, edges are 1px slate lines, and nothing glows. Cyan is the single accent and is spent on selection, the focus ring, the active nav item, tags and trend. The only other colour that appears is severity, and it never appears alone: every severity colour travels with a text label, so the console reads in greyscale.

The density is dense but calm, for an analyst triaging on a laptop and for examiners watching a live run. Numbers are tabular, identifiers (IPs, hashes, ids, event types) are monospace, everything else is the sans face.
keyCharacteristics: Navy ground, one cyan accent, severity colours reserved for severity.
Flat: depth is tonal layering plus 1px borders, no shadows, no glow, no gradients.
Source Sans Pro for text, Source Code Pro only for identifiers, tabular numerals for counts.
Colour is always backed by a text label.

rules.name: The Severity-Only Loudness Rule
rules.body: Warm and red hues mean severity and nothing else. A KPI figure takes its severity colour only when the count is above zero; zero stays neutral so colour means something when it appears.

rules.name: The Label Beside Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour that carries meaning (severity, incident status, health) is always accompanied by its word: badge text, pill text, KPI label.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only accent. Neutral data (counts by source) uses the dimmed cyan, never a second hue.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for identifiers and values only, never for headings, labels or prose.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Counts and scores use tabular numerals and right alignment in tables.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface is distinguished by its panel tone and border, never by a shadow or glow. Hover and active states change tone or border colour only.

dos: Do keep severity colours bound to severity and always show the label word beside them.
Do draw every colour from the token set in `theme.py` so CSS, badges and charts agree.
Do use mono for identifiers only and tabular numerals for counts.
Do keep panels flat: Panel fill, 1px Slate Border, 10px radius.
Do label times as UTC and the score as an experimental prioritisation score.
Do keep focus visible with the 2px cyan outline.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue or use warm colours for anything but severity.
Don't add shadows, glow, gradients or decorative widgets.
Don't carry meaning by colour alone.
Don't put raw colours in inline styles; Streamlit strips them, so colour travels as a class (`sev-*`, `st-*`).
